newsitem.title: USA: Tejas president joins Houston Industries.
newsitem.headline: Tejas president joins Houston Industries.

text.p: Tejas Gas Corp on Friday said President and Chief Operating Officer Charles Crisp left the company to join Houston Lighting and Power, the utility subsidiary of Houston Industries Inc.
An HL&P spokesman said Crisp will become executive vice president and general manager responsible for the company's 13,000 megawatt fossil fuel generating capacity.

"He'll also be responsible for natural gas procurement and our regulated wholesale power trading," the HL&P spokesman said. Crisp will be involved in expanding the utility's fledgling non-regulated power wholesale operation, he said.
The duties of Tejas president were assumed by Jay Precourt, who will continue as vice chairman and chief executive officer, the Houston-based natural gas company said.

Crisp will be replaced on the board of Coral Energy LP by James Whalen, who was named Tejas senior executive vice president. Coral is Tejas' North American energy marketing joint venture with Shell Oil Co, a unit of Royal Dutch/Shell Group.

Precourt said the loss of Crisp will not have an impact on the company's growth plans. "The company remains positioned to implement our aggressive growth strategy," which includes capital expansion plans in Oklahoma, growth of the Coral venture and acquisitions, he said.
